title: Sentiment Analysis Using Large Language Models : A Review
abstract: Sentiment analysis is an important Natural Language Processing (NLP) task for identifying opinions, attitudes, and emotional polarity in user-generated text.Recent research has examined Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT, Gemini, GPT-4, LLaMA, and related models for zero-shot, few-shot, prompt-based, multilingual, and aspectbased sentiment analysis.Compared with conventional supervised approaches, LLMs provide flexible naturallanguage task formulation, but published studies also report challenges related to consistency, domain adaptation, multilingual performance, fine-grained classification, sarcasm, explainability, and computational cost This paper presents a review of sentiment analysis using Large Language Models, with particular attention to user reviews and the analysis of generative-AI applications.The review covers traditional feature-based methods, LLM prompting and classification approaches, multilingual and aspect-based sentiment analysis, and application-oriented review mining.A five-class sentiment frameworkvery negative, negative, neutral, positive, and very positiveis considered as a fine-grained alternative to binary classification.The review further identifies research gaps involving binary-class limitations, dataset size and diversity, domain adaptation, and reliable evaluation.These observations motivate the proposed study of Google Gemini mobile-application reviews using TF-IDF and machinelearning classifiers, with evaluation through Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1-score.

title: Verification Companion for the Revised Orthogonal-Circle Ruled Surface v5
abstract: Verification companion to Akari Hayami (Jian-Yu Huang), The Orthogonal-Circle Ruled Surface: A Boundary Atlas, Five Rank Singularities, and Conditional Fold-Signal Recurrence (v5; paper DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23073642). New in version 0.04 (research beyond the published article): the global self-intersection is classified. On the closed parameter rectangle, distinct labels of S(t,u) = (c + 2u(1-c), (1-u) sin t, u sqrt(c(2-c))), c = cos t, share an image exactly on the u = 1 seam or on two mirror double arcs. title: CGAT-PAD: A Consistency-Guided Anomaly Transformer for Photovoltaic Anomaly Detection
abstract: With the large-scale deployment of photovoltaic (PV) systems, time-series anomaly detection (TSAD) in PV operation data has become important for maintaining operational safety and energy yield. In practical PV scenarios, anomaly labels are scarce, and unsupervised anomaly detection (UAD) methods are often affected by low-quality training data and insufficient modeling of multivariate physical coupling. To address these challenges, this paper proposes the Consistency-Guided Anomaly Transformer for Photovoltaic Anomaly Detection (CGAT-PAD). The Tri-domain Consistency Assessment Module (TCAM) evaluates training-sample quality in the time, frequency, and residual domains, using physically grouped synchronous perturbation augmentation to support the generation of a consistency index. The Consistency-Guided Anomaly Transformer (CGAT) then incorporates this index into the Anomaly Transformer (AT) training loss as an adaptive weight, thereby down-weighting low-quality samples while retaining useful normal patterns. A controlled evaluation benchmark is constructed from real Photovoltaic Data Acquisition (PVDAQ) operation records by injecting reproducible synthetic anomalies into the test segment. Evaluation using F1, F1 PA%K , and AUC shows that CGAT-PAD outperforms the compared baselines, indicating the value of tri-domain consistency guidance for robust detection in nonstationary PV data.

title: The accuracy–utility gap: Why AI accuracy does not guarantee clinical benefit in digital pathology
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in digital pathology has repeatedly achieved expert-level diagnostic accuracy under controlled validation conditions. However, its clinical translation—reflected in regulatory approval, routine adoption, changes in diagnostic decisions, or demonstrated patient benefit—remains inconsistent. This viewpoint argues that this discrepancy arises because diagnostic accuracy is a property of a model under specified conditions, whereas clinical utility emerges from the entire sociotechnical pathway in which the model is deployed. Building on recent work on standardization, system selection, institutional validation, and trial governance, we integrate these complementary layers into a continuous tissue-to-outcome pathway comprising six stages: tissue, image, model, workflow, decision, and outcome, with each stage explicitly linked to the claim it can support. Variability introduced at any stage may remain undetected and propagate downstream, potentially affecting clinical decisions and patient care. Accordingly, evidence generated at one stage cannot substitute for that required to support claims at subsequent stages. We therefore propose a stage-linked evidence map that identifies the principal risk and evidence required at each stage, while making explicit which stronger downstream claims remain unsupported. This framework enables reviewers and institutions considering adoption to identify where a study has addressed the accuracy–utility gap and where uncertainty remains. Evaluating AI across the complete pathway reframes the evidentiary requirements for clinical translation: high diagnostic accuracy is necessary, but insufficient, to establish meaningful clinical utility.

title: Exploring the risks of generative AI misuse via ambiguous prompts: Bypassing safety filters in Text-to-Image/Video models
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) has introduced new textual and multimedia data generation capabilities. Recently, several new Text-to-Image/Video (T2I/V) models have been released, demonstrating advanced capabilities in generating realistic images and video from textual prompts. These models have been conceived to maximize their usability across a broad audience, ensuring that users with varying levels of domain expertise can easily interact with them. However, many of these models often fail to meet comprehensive safety criteria, leaving significant gaps in their ability to prevent the generation of unethical or harmful content. This lack of robust safeguards increases the risk that such tools may be misused, intentionally or unintentionally, to produce media that violates ethical standards or propagates misinformation. This research explores the ethical implications of emerging T2I/V models by investigating their ability to generate unethical multimedia content, such as that containing stereotypes, prejudice, violence, and discrimination. To this end, we employ ambiguous prompts, which are seemingly benign or neutral prompts but can be crafted by domain-expert users to bypass the models’ safety mechanisms and indirectly provoke the generation of harmful content. Through user analysis and the evaluation of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) like Claude and Gemini, we find that, while many T2I/V models are designed to avoid generating unethical content, they still produce a significant amount of discriminatory and stereotypical media. A complementary user study involving 50 participants further shows that such content is widely perceived as offensive, non-inclusive, and unsuitable for younger or vulnerable audiences. Conversely, the results demonstrate that Claude Sonnet and Gemini 1.5 Pro show a moderate but promising capacity to analyze and identify unethical elements within multimedia content.

title: Hypothesis-guided discovery of cognitive algorithms via program refinement
abstract: Developing cognitive models of algorithmic reasoning from behavioral data is a central problem in cognitive science that challenges current methods. Traditional approaches to cognitive modeling are interpretable and benefit from human expertise, but lack flexibility and scalability. Emerging techniques using large language models (LLMs) for de novo generation of cognitive models are scalable and flexible, but lack a role for human expertise and have mostly been applied to simpler tasks than algorithm recovery. We propose a hybrid system that treats discovery of cognitive algorithms as a program refinement problem. Human-created cognitive models are expressed as probabilistic programs and provided to a system of LLM agents with a mandate to: identify mismatches between model and behavior; propose code-level modifications within researcher-specified constraints; and verify structural fidelity. Revisions propagate to a probabilistic inference module that performs inference for latent variables and data likelihood computations. We evaluate the pipeline on human behavior in a problem-solving paradigm that exposes a variety of cognitive algorithms. Revised models consistently improve model fit relative to ancestral models and reveal a small set of recurring innovations that capture meaningful behavioral variability in this task.

title: Detecting Inconsistencies in Model Specifications with LLM-as-Verifier Reasoning
abstract: Model specifications define how large language models (LLMs) should behave, guiding alignment training, inference-time behavior, and evaluation. Yet these specifications may themselves contain defects: two individually reasonable principles may prescribe incompatible behavior when applied to the same situation, leaving no response that satisfies both. Detecting such inconsistencies is challenging. Formalizing natural-language specifications risks losing subtle distinctions, while behavior-based testing cannot reliably distinguish specification defects from differences in model behavior. We introduce VeriSpec, the first approach to directly detect inconsistencies in model specifications by auditing the specification text itself. Our key insight is to preserve the specification in natural language while using an LLM as a verifier. VeriSpec extracts structured, context-aware rules, constructs a topic-guided graph to cluster behaviorally related rules at the same authority level, and applies LLM-as-verifier reasoning to detect inconsistencies. Applying VeriSpec to the OpenAI Model Spec, we extract 405 rules and manually validate five inconsistencies, all reported to its developers, who responded positively and have initiated internal discussions. Compared with five baselines, VeriSpec identifies the most validated inconsistencies, achieves the highest precision (38.5%), and incurs the lowest cost per validated inconsistency ($11.12). These results establish direct specification auditing as a practical complement to behavioral alignment evaluation, catching defects at the source before they shape any model. The code is available at https://github.com/HIPREL-Group/VeriSpec.

title: Unflattening by Flattening -- How Input Distributions Shape Output Variance in Angle-Encoded Circuits
abstract: Barren plateaus hinder training of parameterized quantum circuits by making loss gradients exponentially small in the number of qubits. For angle-encoded product states, we show how the input distribution affects output variation through algebraic input purity, i.e. the input's overlap with the circuit's dynamical Lie algebra. With the specified readouts and Haar or exact group 2-design sampling, matchgate circuits on $n$ qubits retain output variance of order $1/n$ for every pure product input. The off-diagonal family instead has zero output on computational-basis inputs at any depth and for every parameter choice. Independent uniform angles yield mean variance of the same order as matchgates. A count of diagonal Pauli strings identifies these zero-output endpoints. For any fixed dataset of nonzero inputs with at least $2n$ coordinates, we construct a classical preprocessing certificate. A shared random rotation is accepted only when the dataset's mean purity passes a computable threshold. This certifies mean output variance of order $1/n$ for the off-diagonal family before circuit execution, with a constant expected number of trials. Binary and ternary weighted encodings also recover the independent-angle mean purity from one uniform scalar input. Numerical experiments examine training behavior and extensions to larger algebras. The guarantee concerns output variance averaged over inputs, while successful learning also depends on the task and information preserved by the encoding.

title: Clock Diffusion: Efficient Semi-Autoregressive Continuous Diffusion Language Models
abstract: Recent works on continuous diffusion for discrete data have demonstrated performance on par with comparable discrete diffusion models. However, these continuous counterparts lack key features that are essential to practical use as language models, namely variable-length generation and support for a key-value cache, and they still lag behind the frontier of autoregressive and discrete diffusion quality. In this work, we address these limitations. We do so by introducing a model parameterization that uses position-dependent noise schedules to define semi-autoregressive (SAR) continuous diffusion language models (DLMs). Together with efficient training and sampling algorithms, we call this framework Clock Diffusion, and we present two special cases of our method: block and sliding window generation. We then define ClockDLMs, a family of Gaussian DLMs based on sliding window Clock Diffusion that attain state-of-the-art diffusion likelihood bounds on OpenWebText, even beating the performant block SAR discrete diffusion models. ClockDLMs trained on TinyGSM also substantially outperform continuous baselines on the GSM8K benchmark and match and exceed comparable SAR discrete diffusion models. Finally, building on our parameterization, we propose more efficient samplers that we dub Cache Grab, which adapt techniques from accelerated inference in discrete diffusion, such as committing tokens whose probabilities exceed a confidence threshold and self-speculative decoding, further improving our models' quality and efficiency.

title: Unitary fault-tolerant encoding of Pauli states in surface codes
abstract: In fault-tolerant quantum computation, the preparation of logical states is a ubiquitous subroutine, yet significant challenges persist even for the simplest states required. In the present work, we present a unitary, scalable, distance-preserving encoding scheme for preparing Pauli eigenstates in surface codes. Unlike previous unitary approaches whose fault-distance remains constant with increasing code distance, our scheme ensures that the protection offered by the code is preserved during state preparation. Building on strategies discovered by reinforcement learning for the surface-17 code, we generalize the construction to arbitrary code distances and both rotated and unrotated surface codes. The proposed encoding relies only on geometrically local gates, and is therefore fully compatible with planar 2D qubit connectivity, and it achieves circuit depth scaling as O ( d ), consistent with fundamental entanglement-generation bounds. We design explicit stabilizer-expanding circuits with and without ancilla-mediated connectivity and analyze their error-propagation behavior. Numerical simulations under depolarizing noise show that our unitary encoding without ancillas outperforms standard stabilizer-measurement-based schemes, reducing logical error rates by up to an order of magnitude. These results make the scheme particularly relevant for platforms such as trapped ions and neutral atoms, where measurements are costly relative to gates and idling noise is considerably weaker than gate noise. Our work bridges the gap between measurement-based and unitary encodings of surface-code states and opens new directions for distance-preserving state preparation in fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: RS-2026-083 - Why We Built Our Own: Design Rationale for a From-Scratch Agentic AI Security Control Plane
abstract: Agent frameworks have become critical infrastructure, yet they were not designed as security boundaries. This paper documents the design rationale for a from-scratch agentic AI security control plane built independently of any third-party agent framework. We present the requirements that forced the build, the architecture that resulted, and seven months of production operation across 50+ security modules across 17 verticals. We position our work against prior art — OATS, LICITRA-SENTRY, DROS-6P, Ring Zero, and AgentWard — and identify the gap: a production-tested implementation that owns cryptographic evidence chains, native action gating, and a runtime kill switch within a single architecture.

title: Confidence-Aware Autonomous Knowledge Graph Evolution for Lifelong Robotic TAMP Systems
abstract: Neuro-symbolic Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) architectures anchor Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning within a Knowledge Graph (KG) K to eliminate plan-level hallucinations, but letting K evolve autonomously across missions risks contaminating it with confidently-wrong facts that both the planner and the perception stack will then trust. We formalize this problem and address it with a unified Autonomous Knowledge Update framework combining confidence-aware entity-attribute belief fusion, geolocated obstacle ingestion, and density-based emergence of Zones of Interest, all governed by the same hybrid syntactic-semantic Dempster-Shafer fusion rule so that contamination resistance is a property of the framework ratherthan of any single channel. We give a full algorithmic specification of its three update channels and a field evaluation over 8-mission made in a EU H2020 OLGA project context deployment that shows obstacle-driven mid-mission replanning triggers falling from 10 to 0 events, KG growth correlating with plan richness at r = 0.993, our fusion mechanism keeping contamination roughly an order of magnitude lower than a naive last-write-wins updater across tested observation error rates, and cross-checking the on-board recognition module against K raising its top-1 accuracy from 89.7% to 94.0% over the campaign.

We formalize this problem and address it with a unified Autonomous Knowledge Update framework combining confidence-aware entity-attribute belief fusion, geolocated obstacle ingestion, and density-based emergence of Zones of Interest, all governed by the same hybrid syntactic-semantic Dempster-Shafer fusion rule so that contamination resistance is a property of the framework ratherthan of any single channel. We give a full algorithmic specification of its three update channels and a field evaluation over 8-mission made in a EU H2020 OLGA project context deployment that shows obstacle-driven mid-mission replanning triggers falling from 10 to 0 events, KG growth correlating with plan richness at r = 0.993, our fusion mechanism keeping contamination roughly an order of magnitude lower than a naive last-write-wins updater across tested observation error rates, and cross-checking the on-board recognition module against K raising its top-1 accuracy from 89.7% to 94.0% over the campaign.

title: Generative AI in Fashion E-Commerce Product Imagery: An Experimental Test of Image Origin and Transparency Labelling on Consumer Trust, Perceived Product Quality and Purchase Intention
abstract: Retailers are increasingly replacing photographic model shoots with synthetic product imagery generated by text-to-image systems, a deployment decision that couples substantial production savings with an unresolved question about consumer response and about the transparency obligations attached to synthetic content. This study examines how AI-generated and photographic product images are evaluated in fashion e-commerce and how a visible origin label affects that evaluation. A 2 (image origin: AI-generated vs. photograph) × 2 (labelling: absent vs. present) between-subjects online experiment was conducted with 150 participants. Consumer trust, perceived product quality and purchase intention were measured with established scales, and general attitude toward artificial intelligence was tested as a moderator. Without labelling, no statistically significant differences between the two image types emerged on any dependent variable. The visible label reduced perceived product quality significantly but modestly, while effects on trust and purchase intention, the image origin by label interaction and moderation were not statistically significant.

title: Corpus Poisoning Method for RAG Systems Based on Monte Carlo Tree Search
authors: LI Bohan, CAI Manchun, ZHANG Teng
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems enhance the timeliness and factual consistency of large language models (LLMs) by incorporating an external knowledge base. However, this structure also makes them highly vulnerable to corpus poisoning attacks, particularly in black-box scenarios where internal model parameters are inaccessible. To address the challenge of constructing adversarial passages that can approximate target queries in the embedding space under black-box conditions, this paper proposes an attack framework for RAG corpus poisoning based on structured search. Specifically, the framework models the adversarial sample construction as a high-dimensional combinatorial optimization problem in the discrete text space. It introduces Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) to enable global planning of candidate token sequences and leverages a dynamic vocabulary generated by GPT-4o to enhance the search??s semantic relevance and efficiency. The resulting adversarial passage is then injected into the knowledge base and iteratively refined through validation, achieving stable retrieval hijacking in a black-box setting. Systemic experiments on multiple benchmark datasets and various sizes of Qwen2.5 models demonstrate the robust attack performance of the proposed framework, achieving an average retrieval hijack status at Rank 1 of 89.0% and a final answer contamination status of 83.9%. Experimental results demonstrate that, without requiring gradient information or access to internal model parameters, the proposed method effectively optimizes retrieval ranking signals through structured search, achieving higher attack success rates and better stealthiness than existing heuristic-based approaches.

title: Assessment of Global Horizontal Irradiance Data Quality and Calibration Uncertainty in a Tropical Monsoon Region: A Case Study in Kamphaeng Phet, Thailand
abstract: Ground-based solar radiation data are useful for environmental studies and solar-energy assessment, especially in tropical monsoon regions where sky conditions change throughout the year. This study investigated the quality and variability of hourly global horizontal irradiance (GHI) measured at Kamphaeng Phet Rajabhat University, Thailand, from January to December 2025. GHI was measured using an SMP10-V thermopile pyranometer. The instrument recorded data every 5 s, and the data were later averaged into hourly values. The dataset was checked by separating daylight hours, assessing data availability, and applying preliminary physical range screening. Nighttime periods were not treated as missing data, and no gap filling was performed. During the study period, 4,420 daylight hourly records were expected. Of these, 4,355 records were available and passed the physical range screening, giving an overall daylight-data availability of 98.53%. The record-weighted annual mean hourly GHI was 404.63 W/m2. Monthly mean GHI ranged from 322.50 W/m2 in July to 474.36 W/m2 in March. The seasonal results showed that mean GHI was highest in summer and lowest in the rainy season. The rainy season also showed the highest relative variability because atmospheric conditions were more variable during this period. The pyranometer calibration certificate reported an expanded calibration uncertainty of 1.39% at k=2. These results provide a local reference for measured GHI characteristics and data-quality evaluation in a tropical monsoon environment.

title: The Choose-Your-Own-Adventure Calculus
abstract: In many programming systems, the user can interactively construct a program by repeatedly triggering a completion mechanism and choosing one of the offered options. This is the case with code editors for object-oriented languages (choosing a member), data exploration environments (choosing a transformation), but also with theorem provers (choosing a tactic) and structure editors (choosing a grammar~rule).

title: NEEDLEWORK: Offline Rewriting of Robot Data with Verified Local Stitches
abstract: Robot demonstrations may contain useful behavior even when individual episodes are inefficient or unsuccessful. Trajectory stitching offers a way to compose these behaviors into improved training data, but identifying useful connections and verifying their feasibility is difficult in high-dimensional robot data, where many prior methods rely on low-dimensional state representations. We introduce NEEDLE, an offline dataset-augmentation algorithm that addresses these challenges by adding short, verified action bridges between recorded observations in high-dimensional robot demonstrations. First, NEEDLE identifies and creates connections that bypass suboptimal detours, broaden action coverage, and augment the original dataset with failed trajectories, using only RGB images, proprioception, and episode-level outcomes, without new environment interaction or privileged object state. Next, we present a sampling technique that incorporates accepted bridges into policy training without synthesizing intermediate images or discarding the original demonstrations, allowing policies to learn alternative actions while retaining the original dataset's coverage. On real-robot tasks, NEEDLE improves success rate over the strongest baseline on each task by an average of 21 percentage points. Videos and supplementary materials are on https://needle-work.github.io/.

title: Learnt Attacks on Quantum Key Distribution under Channel Noise and Device Drift
abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) links are provisioned from security analyses of stationary channels, whereas the devices that determine the channel drift between recalibrations. Whether an eavesdropper who cannot alter the channel's own noise gains by following that drift has not been quantified. Adaptive eavesdropping is posed here as a constrained Markov decision process in which the attacker selects one circuit per round while the noise level follows an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process and the abort condition is a budget over each block of rounds. The value of adaptation is bounded by the best fixed circuit and a dynamic-programming upper bound. The actions are learnt attacks. Whereas Decker et al. trained a parametrised circuit on a fixed gate template against a fixed channel, here the gate structure and rotation angles are searched jointly. This yields circuits compact enough to form a discrete action set, extending the construction to noise models lacking a known template, including the amplitude damping channel. On device-independent E91 under bilateral depolarising noise, a reinforcement-learning attacker raises her Holevo information from $0.135$ for the best fixed circuit to $0.348$ at zero detection, $98\%$ of the upper bound. On BB84 under a drifting bit-flip channel, she exceeds a conservative noise-indexed rule by $0.024$ in fidelity, reaching $99\%$ of the upper bound. Under stationary noise, the attacker's gain from basis asymmetry changes sign between an averaged and a per-basis error-rate constraint. The search, started from random gate sequences, recovers the analytical cloners and the collective-attack key rate, and meets the lower bound of the Winick--Lütkenhaus--Coles objective from above.

title: Who Thinks First? Designing Productive Friction with Engage-to-Unlock GenAI
abstract: Generative AI can support writing, but frictionless access may cause cognitive offloading before users develop their own ideas. We introduce Engage-to-Unlock, a productive-friction mechanism that unlocks generative capabilities after users meaningfully engage with the task. In a controlled experiment (N = 398), participants completed a writing task under one of four conditions: Human-Only, Standard Chatbot, Engage-to-Unlock, or Time-Matched Unlock, which matched unlock timing to Engage-to-Unlock participants but independent of users' engagement, then evaluated passages for evidence and inferential errors. Results show that Engage-to-Unlock redistributed effort across tasks: participants spent more time writing and less time evaluating, without increasing overall task duration. They also submitted more prompts than in other AI-assisted conditions and showed the highest accuracy-per-time evaluation efficiency across conditions. These findings suggest that designing GenAI access to encourage early human engagement may provide a productive form of friction, while retaining active AI use and efficient downstream evaluation.

title: JoinGR: Learning to Traverse Join Graphs for Table Retrieval
abstract: Retrieving the right tables is a prerequisite for Text-to-SQL over realistic databases. Dense table retrievers rank schema elements independently, but this ignores a key source of evidence: some required tables are not mentioned in the question and become identifiable only through their join relationships to already relevant tables. We introduce JOINGR, a join-aware table retrieval method that treats the database join graph as the retrieval space. Columns are represented as graph nodes, while intra-table and foreign-key relationships are represented as typed edges. Given a question, JOINGR selects semantically similar anchor tables, traverses join edges with a query-conditioned scorer, and aggregates the resulting edge deposits into table scores. The scorer is a lightweight MLP on top of frozen query, node, and edge embeddings, trained with a pairwise margin loss over gold tables. On BIRD and Spider datasets, JOINGR is competitive with the strongest retrieval baselines. On BEAVER, a challenging enterprise benchmark with multi-hop table requirements, JOINGR substantially improves recall over dense retrieval and re-ranking baselines. Cross-domain experiments show that the learned scorer transfers across benchmarks, indicating that the method captures reusable joingraph traversal behavior.

title: Towards Retrieval Augmented Generation in High-Energy and Astroparticle Physics
abstract: The high-energy and astroparticle physics literature has grown into an enormous body of knowledge. Gaining a comprehensive understanding of this literature is an important step in research, but is a challenging task. Before making meaningful advances, it is important to establish what has already been done and identify open questions. However, this process is becoming increasingly difficult given the sheer volume of publications. Conducting a focused literature survey on a narrow topic is particularly challenging. We develop an open-source Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline to produce concise, targeted summary reports with citations, grounded in the database of arXiv papers, enabling researchers, editors, and referees to rapidly orient themselves within any corner of the field. Specifically, we embed approximately 230K hep-ph and astro-ph.HE papers to enable a hybrid retrieval that captures both keyword matches and semantic similarity. The fused candidate set is then refined using a cross-encoder reranker. Following retrieval, the papers are passed to a Large Language Model (LLM), for which we use Google DeepMind's open-source Gemma-4-E4B model. The LLM first acts as a judge to evaluate the relevance and then synthesizes a coherent and grounded report with references. This modern AI-driven approach allows us to go beyond the capabilities of classical keyword search on arXiv or Inspire-HEP.

title: Universal Dilation of Linear Itô SDEs: Quantum Trajectories and Lindblad Simulation of Second Moments
abstract: We present a universal framework for simulating N -dimensional linear Itô stochastic differential equations (SDEs) on quantum computers with additive or multiplicative noises. Building on a unitary dilation technique, we establish a rigorous mapping from the general linear SDEs d X t = A ( t ) X t d t + ∑ j = 1 J B j ( t ) X t d W t j to stochastic Schrödinger equations (SSE) on a dilated Hilbert space. Crucially, this embedding is pathwise exact in that the classical solution is recovered as a projection of the dilated quantum state for each fixed noise realization. We demonstrate that the resulting SSEs are naturally implementable on digital quantum processors, where the stochastic Wiener increments are encoded directly by preparing the ancillary qubits. Exploiting this physical mapping, we develop two algorithmic strategies: (1) a trajectory-based approach that uses sequential weak measurements to realize efficient stochastic integrators, including a second-order scheme, and (2) an ensemble-based approach that maps moment evolution to a deterministic Lindblad quantum master equation, enabling simulation without Monte Carlo sampling. We provide error bounds based on a stochastic light-cone analysis and validate the framework with numerical experiments.

title: الابتكار في البحث العلمي المدعوم بالذكاء الاصطناعي الوكيل: الاتجاهات والتطبيقات والتحديات الناشئة
abstract: يتناول البحث الابتكار في البحث العلمي المدعوم بالذكاء الاصطناعي الوكيل، في ضوء الانتقال من استخدام الذكاء الاصطناعي بوصفه أداة مساعدة إلى أنظمة قادرة على التخطيط، واستخدام الأدوات، وتنفيذ مهام بحثية مترابطة بدرجات متفاوتة من الاستقلالية. ويهدف إلى تأصيل مفهوم الذكاء الاصطناعي الوكيل، وتحليل تطبيقاته في مراحل البحث العلمي، وبيان أبرز تحدياته المنهجية والعلمية والحوكمية. واعتمد البحث المنهج الوصفي التحليلي من خلال مراجعة الأدبيات العلمية الحديثة ذات الصلة وتحليل اتجاهاتها وتطبيقاتها. وأظهرت النتائج أن الذكاء الاصطناعي الوكيل يختلف عن الاستخدام التقليدي للذكاء الاصطناعي التوليدي بقدرته على إدارة مهام متعددة نحو هدف محدد، وأن تطبيقاته تمتد من توليد الأفكار والفرضيات إلى الاكتشاف والتحليل العلمي والتجريب المؤتمت والمختبرات ذاتية القيادة. كما تبين أن زيادة استقلالية هذه الأنظمة ترافقها تحديات تتعلق بدقة المخرجات، وانتقال الأخطاء بين مراحل التنفيذ، وقابلية التتبع والتحقق، والنزاهة العلمية، وتحديد المسؤولية. وخلص البحث إلى أن القيمة الحقيقية للذكاء الاصطناعي الوكيل لا تكمن في استبدال الباحث، بل في إعادة تنظيم سير العمل البحثي ضمن تكامل منضبط بين القدرات الوكيلية والحكم العلمي البشري. ويوصي البحث بالتحقق البشري من المراحل الجوهرية، وتوثيق استخدام الأنظمة الوكيلية، وتقييم العملية البحثية كاملة، وتحديد مستويات واضحة لتفويض المهام وفق طبيعتها ومخاطرها. كما يدعو إلى دراسات تقارن أداء الباحث والنظام الوكيلي والعمل المشترك بينهما في مراحل البحث المختلفة.

title: Mitigating Cascading Prompt Injections in Multi-Agent Systems via Semantic Boundary Mediation and Observability
abstract: The rapid industrial adoption of autonomous agentic workflows on cloud-native platforms has shifted the primary cybersecurity attack surface from model-layer alignment to system-layer execution privileges. This research identifies and analyses the emerging threat of Cascading Prompt Injections (CPI) within multi-agent systems (MAS). In a CPI scenario, a compromised or manipulated “Supervisor Agent” propagates malicious, high-privilege instructions to downstream “Worker Agents” that possess broad execution scopes, bypassing traditional input-layer guardrails. We demonstrate that existing safety filters are ineffective against these inter-agent escalations due to the “Confused Deputy” vulnerability inherent in default service account configurations. To address this, we introduce the Semantic Boundary Framework (SBF), a zero-trust architectural mediation layer implemented on Google Cloud Platform (GCP). The SBF utilizes an event-driven verification proxy to measure “Intent Drift” between the user’s original prompt and the resulting worker-level API calls. By applying geometric vector analysis via Vertex AI Vector Search, the framework mathematically validates the congruency of agentic actions in real-time. Experimental results using a three-tier swarm on Vertex AI show a 74% increase in the detection of cross-agent privilege escalation while introducing a negligible mean latency of 58ms. This paper provides a scalable roadmap to implement semantic-aware security in autonomous cloud ecosystems without sacrificing operational performance.

title: Data from Radiometer (RAD) measurements at Paris – Chemin Vert Bobigny (PACHEM) from 2023-06-29 to 2024-03-04 [L0]
abstract: Combined and uncalibrated logger data from radiometer measurements on a sun tracker with global, direct and diffuse shortwave irradiance and longwave irradiance at Paris – Chemin Vert Bobigny (PACHEM) (Département 93) in the urbanized area in the NE of Greater Paris recorded during the urbisphere Paris Campaign from 2023-06-29 00:00 to 2024-03-05 00:00 UTC. Measuerments were taken at roof level on top of a residential high-rise buiding at 48.904672°N / 2.4447328°E. The L0 datafile combines all individual uncalibrated logger files (automatic transfer, manual download) with a consistent and consecutive time axis. Missing data is filled with -9999. The data file has each time step as a row and each parameter as a column in comma-separated csv format. The columns contain readings converted to physical units with simple quality control from all radiometers and a co-located all-in one automatic weather station (AWS). The file PACHEM-MET_1min-202306290000_202403050000_UTC.csv has the format of a comma-separated .csv file with 4 header lines following the Campbell Scientific Inc. TOA5 file definition. The L0 data combined all raw data files into a single .csv file covering the entire period of observations at PAAUNA from 2023-06-29 00:00 to 2024-03-05 11:03 UTC based on RAW data averaged every minute. RAW data (individual logger output files) can be found here: Morrison, W., Hilland, R., Looschelders, D., Zeeman, M., Grimmond, S., & Christen, A. (2024). Data from Radiometer (RAD) measurements at Paris – Chemin Vert Bobigny (PACHEM) from 2023-06-28 to 2024-03-04 [RAW] (Version v1.0.2) [Dataset]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.12967485 Radiation measurements taken at PACHEM are: Direct normal irradiance (DNI) with an CHP1 pyrheliometer Global (solar) hemispherical irradiance (GHI) with an actively ventilated Kipp&Zonen CM21 pyranometer Diffuse (solar) irradiance with an actively ventilated and shaded Kipp&Zonen CM21 pyranometer Longwave hemispherical irradiance (LHI) with an actively ventilated and shaded Kipp&Zonen CG1 pyrgeometer All radiation fluxes are measured using a sun tracker (Kipp & Zonen SOLYS2) and continuously ventilated instruments. Further, the dataset contains simple meteorological measurements of barometric pressure, wind velocity, wind direction, air temperature, humidity, precipitation and lightning using a all-in-one weather station (Campbell Scientific ClimaVue 50) installed next to the sun tracker. The dataset is calibrated using manufacturer calibrations for all instruments and no further quality controlls or gap filling procedures have been applied. For quality controlled and calibrated data use L2 data instead. based on air temperature and relative humidity measured with an all-in-one weather sensor (Campbell Scientific ClimaVue50) MET_CV50_VapPressDeficit_hPa_Avg: Vapour pressure deficit in hPa calculated based on air temperature and relative humidity measured with an all-in-one weather sensor (Campbell Scientific ClimaVue50) MET_CV50_MixingRatio_gKg_Avg: Mixing ratio in g/kg calculated based on air title: SentryLine: Reviewable Capability Traces for CPython Plugin Hosts
abstract: SentryLine makes CPython plugin admission explainable at the boundary. The host declares which authority a plugin may exercise; SentryLine records attempted authority classes and reports or rejects the first forbidden prefix before the instrumented effect is allowed to proceed. In the packaged evaluation, the combined monitor preserves all 28 benign workloads, blocks all 72 misuse workloads, and checks 13,888 boundary decisions with zero independent-contract disagreements and zero witnessless rejections. Audit-only monitoring blocks 38 of 72 misuse workloads, which is why the poster shows both interpreter-side and wrapper-side evidence. SentryLine is an admission-time review tool, not a universal Python sandbox.

title: Quantum-compatible error correction using a Bayesian Dual-Gated ProbSparse transformer in discrete-variable quantum key distribution
abstract: Abstract Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) enables secure key generation with information-theoretic security guaranteed by the principles of quantum mechanics. However, achieving high reconciliation efficiency, high throughput, and low frame error rates under noisy channel conditions remains a significant challenge for practical and cost-effective Discrete-Variable Quantum Key Distribution (DV-QKD) systems. To address this issue, this research proposes a Quantum-based Bayesian Dual-Gated ProbSparse Transformer (Q-BDPT) framework for quantum-compatible error correction during the reconciliation stage of DV-QKD. Initially, a system model for DV-QKD is presented. Subsequently, an adaptive error-correction framework comprising Deep-Q-Encoder and Deep-Q-Decoder modules is developed. Unlike physical quantum error-correction codes that operate directly on qubits, the proposed framework processes measurement-derived error features, syndrome information, and channel-dependent error characteristics obtained after quantum-state transmission and measurement. The Deep-Q-Encoder and Deep-Q-Decoder are constructed using Q-BDPT with Binary Cross Entropy (BCE) loss. The proposed Q-BDPT integrates Bayesian Adversarial ProbSparse Transformer (BAPT) and Dual-Gated Spatiotemporal Attention Network (DSANet), while harmonic analysis is employed to enhance feature integration and adaptive error modelling. The framework learns probabilistic, spatial, and temporal error dependencies associated with quantum-channel behavior and generates adaptive reconciliation decisions to improve key recovery performance. Experimental results demonstrate that Q-BDPT achieves a minimum Bit Error Rate (BER) of 0.01760, a minimum Logical Error Rate (LER) of 0.00776, and a maximum Secure Key Rate (SKR) of 0.65805, thereby improving reconciliation effectiveness and secure key generation performance in DV-QKD environments.

title: Machine Learning for Predicting Long-Term Outcomes in Neurocritical Care: A sub-analysis from the SYNAPSE-ICU Study
abstract: PURPOSE: Neurocritical conditions present significant challenges in the intensive care unit (ICU), especially during the initial hours. Accurate early risk assessment is essential for guiding acute care and influencing long-term outcomes. This study aims to evaluate the potential of machine learning (ML) models for risk prediction in neurocritical patients. METHODS: This retrospective sub-analysis of the SYNAPSE-ICU Study applied machine learning to predict the 6-month outcome for patients with three different neurocritical conditions: subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), traumatic brain injury (TBI), or intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). Models were trained at ICU admission, ICU day 3, ICU day 7, and Hospital discharge using the H2O framework, including GLM, DRF, GBM, XGBoost, and Stacked Ensembles. Predictive performance was evaluated using AUPRC and AUROC metrics. RESULTS: 2,202 patients were included with a complete data set to predict the 6-month outcome. At 6 months, 836 patients had a favorable outcome (Glasgow Outcome Scale Extended (GOSE) ≥5) and had a significantly higher GOSE at Hospital discharge (p<0.001). Predictive performance (pooled across five multiply-imputed datasets) was highest at ICU admission (AUROC 0.841 [95% CI 0.804-0.878]) and Hospital discharge (AUROC 0.885 [0.845-0.925]), with a transient reduction during the ICU stay (Day 3: AUROC 0.830 [0.789-0.870]; Day 7: AUROC 0.821 [0.777-0.865]). Age was the most important parameter at the respective time points, except for Hospital discharge, where the GOSE at discharge had the highest impact on the 6-month outcome. CONCLUSION: This sub-analysis demonstrates that machine learning models can effectively predict long-term outcomes for neurocritical patients, with accuracy improving from ICU admission to Hospital discharge. GOSE at discharge and age are critical parameters. The findings underscore the potential of ML models to improve prognostic assessments in neurocritical care.

title: MyoPath: A deep learning pipeline for objective morphometric assessment of skeletal muscle biopsies
abstract: Aims Muscle biopsy assessment relies on descriptive features that are difficult to compare across samples. We developed MyoPath to quantify these features and examined their usefulness in clinical biopsies and population-based autopsy material. Methods MyoPath combines Cellpose-SAM and conventional image analysis within QuPath to segment myofibers, fat, nuclei, and connective tissue. We analyzed 478 hematoxylin and eosin images from HuashanMuscle (79 snap-frozen biopsies) and GTEx (399 formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded autopsy samples). Thirty-seven features were summarized by seven pathology indicators. A composite model trained on GTEx healthy and wasting strata was transferred to HuashanMuscle without retraining. Results Segmentation Dice coefficients ranged from 0.87 to 0.95 on annotated cryosections. Nuclear centralization index (NCI) and fiber size coefficient of variation (fiber CV) discriminated myopathy from controls in HuashanMuscle (AUC 0.85 and 0.79) and wasting from healthy donors in GTEx (0.74 and 0.74). Their GTEx associations changed little after age and sex adjustment. The composite achieved AUC 0.788 (95% CI 0.71–0.85) in GTEx and 0.873 (0.78–0.94) in HuashanMuscle. In the latter cohort, mean predicted probability was 0.49 compared with an observed myopathy proportion of 0.79. Conclusions NCI and fiber CV provide interpretable measures of muscle pathology in two distinct tissue settings. MyoPath supports quantitative comparison between groups; clinical severity grading and interpretation of absolute scores require further validation.

title: Log-driven classification of shale lithofacies employing Kolmogorov-Arnold network assisted by conditional generative adversarial network and transfer learning
abstract: Lithofacies classification is essential for stratigraphic interpretation and sedimentological characterization, but remains challenging in shale reservoirs because rapid lithological variations weaken the discriminative capability of conventional well logs. To improve shale lithofacies identification, this study proposes a hybrid classification framework, termed NCA-Bayes-KAN, in which the Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KAN) is used as the core classifier, neighbourhood component analysis (NCA) is employed for feature optimization, and Bayesian optimization (Bayes) is applied for hyper-parameter tuning. Geological and well-logging data from the Ordos Basin were used to evaluate the proposed framework. Five commonly used classifiers, including k-nearest neighbors, support vector machine, random forest, deep neural network, and extreme gradient boosting, were introduced as benchmark models. Experimental results based on accuracy, F1-score, Cohen’s kappa, and area under the curve (AUC) show that NCA-Bayes-KAN consistently outperforms the competing models. Because softmax-based outputs may produce poorly calibrated probabilities, probability calibration was further incorporated to improve the reliability of predicted class probabilities, leading to additional performance improvements. To enhance model generalization, conditional generative adversarial network (CGAN) and transfer learning were integrated into the framework. CGAN was used for data augmentation, while transfer learning enabled the use of pre-learned knowledge from the source well group. The results indicate that NCA-Bayes-KAN combined with probability calibration provides an accurate and reliable solution for shale lithofacies classification within the investigated study area, while CGAN and transfer learning further improve its transferability among the studied wells and well zones.

title: Reliability Stress Tests and Decision-Time Routing for Chest X-ray Vision-Language Models
abstract: Medical vision-language model (VLM) evaluation is sensitive to workflow design, prompting strategy, and benchmark construction, yet most studies treat these factors in isolation. We introduce a reliability stress test for chest X-ray interpretation built on two balanced datasets (a private report-backed set and a curated MIMIC subset). Three medical VLMs (CheXagent, MedGemma-4B, and MedGemma-27B) are evaluated across three prompt styles and two workflows (single-VLM and multi-agent), producing 36 configurations. We show that exact-match accuracy alone can overstate the effectiveness of conservative models that default to "Normal" predictions. Diagnostic reliability also depends heavily on model family and scale: multi-agent reasoning helps some configurations but hurts others. Building on these observations, we propose a decision-time routing framework that selectively escalates to multi-agent inference only when beneficial, improving the cost-quality trade-off over fixed workflows. Our results highlight the need for evaluation protocols that jointly consider prompt sensitivity, failure-mode diversity, and workflow choice before clinical deployment.

title: Learning Many-Body Hamiltonians Using a Local Probe
abstract: Hamiltonian learning provides a systematic framework for reconstructing unknown quantum dynamics. However, existing protocols typically assume direct measurement access to the entire system. With fast single-qubit control and a connected reference backbone, we show that a single measurable qubit suffices to learn all $O(N)$ independent parameters of a bounded-degree two-body Hamiltonian on $N$ qubits at the Heisenberg limit. Crucially, our protocol uses robust SWAP gates synthesized by quantum signal processing, enabling coherent transfer of states evolving under distant Hamiltonian parameters to the measurable qubit. This transfer requires no prior calibration of the Hamiltonian parameters of the intermediate links. A parallel learning architecture achieves total query time $\widetilde{O}(N)$ for an $N$-qubit chain, while retaining Heisenberg-limited precision scaling. On the chain, these scalings match the fundamental precision and information-propagation lower bounds up to logarithmic factors. The framework further extends to arbitrary bounded-degree interaction graphs. Our results establish a scalable route to learning an extensive number of many-body Hamiltonian parameters through only a local measurement interface.

title: Molecular Dynamics with Nuclear Effects on Quantum Computers
abstract: Nuclear quantum effects are critical for describing proton transfer and hydrogen bonding, but their incorporation into quantum chemistry calculations is often computationally prohibitive on classical hardware. A promising alternative are quantum computers due to their linear scaling in the space requirements with system size. We introduce a novel hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for ab-initio molecular dynamics that incorporates nuclear quantum effects via the nuclear-electronic orbital method. The proposed algorithm evaluates ground state energies and forces on the quantum computer using a variational quantum eigensolver, while the molecular geometries are updated classically. We validate our approach through simulations of $\text{H}_2$, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and the Zundel ion $\text{H}_5\text{O}_2^+$, comparing the simulated vibrational spectra with experimental data. Upon inclusion of nuclear quantum effects, the proton shuttling movement in the Zundel ion becomes effectively barrierless, and errors in the simulated frequencies improve significantly. Employing compact hardware-efficient ansatz circuits we achieve results comparable to the more accurate UCCSD ansatzes, which hints towards the feasibility of executing our algorithm on near-term quantum devices.

title: Rethinking the Information Bottleneck: Structured Decomposition under Label-Induced Partitions
abstract: Standard information bottleneck (IB) regularization constrains representations via a single scalar I(Z;X), implicitlytreating all information as homogeneous. However, a single global compression control couples label-relevant structurewith residual within-condition variation, rather than regulating their allocation independently, allowing nuisanceinformation to persist in learned representations. For example, in medical imaging applications, residual variation oftenstems from acquisition conditions, background factors, or subject-specific appearance. This issue becomes particularlypronounced in data-limited settings, where models tend to overfit such variation, hindering generalization. While existingregularization methods can stabilize training, control capacity, or shape representation geometry, they do not explicitlyseparate nuisance-like variation from task-supporting structure. To address this limitation, we revisit IB from a structuredperspective based on a label-induced partition, where condition-level structure and within-condition information playdistinct roles. This leads to a dual-bottleneck formulation: a standard KL term controls global information capacity, while aconditional KL term targets within-condition information. We show that the conditional KL admits an exact decompositioninto a within-condition information term and a prior-mismatch term, explaining its alignment with the design objective.With a simplex-structured conditional prior, the method provides controllable latent geometry and integrates seamlesslyinto existing pipelines. Experiments on classification and segmentation show the clearest gains in low-data classificationand consistent improvements across dense prediction benchmarks.

title: Learning Rate Transfer for Hybrid Transformer-SSM Architectures
abstract: We study learning rate (LR) scaling for hybrid architectures combining Transformer and State-Space Model (SSM) blocks, a class adopted by several recent production language models. In particular, we focus on the gap between the theoretical scaling rules derived for SSMs under zero-order-hold (ZOH) discretization at infinite width with growing state size, and the field-standard practical implementations using simplified-ZOH Mamba at fixed state size. Surprisingly, in this practical regime hybrid architectures achieve a near-zero LR transfer gap across widths 256-2048 and depths 4-32 up to billion-parameter scale using only the original $μ$P prescription, even though SSM operations fall outside its Tensor Programs representability conditions and every parameterization we test fails the standard coordinate-check diagnostic of $μ$P correctness. We attribute this to a two-condition decomposition of LR transfer in hybrid architectures: a global update-to-weight invariance, enforced by $μ$P's initialization and LR scaling; and a local per-component balance, provided by AdamW's per-parameter normalization. Our observations show that the optimal LR is invariant to width up to 8$\times$, that this width invariance holds across depth, sequence length, batch size, and Transformer-to-SSM ratio, and that it transfers to Nemotron-H, a production hybrid outside our custom architecture set. We hope these findings fill the gap between theoretical scaling rules and practical hybrid implementations, and stimulate further research toward bridging it.

title: Semantic Privacy Protection with Utility Preservation for 3D Point Clouds
abstract: Abstract Point cloud data face serious semantic privacy risks during acquisition, transmission, and cross-institutional sharing. Existing methods mostly rely on geometric perturbation or destructive encryption, which can reduce the recognizability of the original class but often impair downstream usability. This paper proposes a class-transfer-based semantic encryption framework for point clouds, aiming to conceal original class information while preserving task utility and supporting authorized recovery. Specifically, we construct a unified latent space with a shared-backbone Normalizing Flow, and combine LoRA and FiLM to achieve parameter-efficient class-conditional adaptation. We further introduce diffusion-guided flow alignment to regularize the latent distribution, construct an energy-based category transition graph, and obtain an optimal class-transfer table through global matching. Then, a latent-space Neural ODE continuously evolves source-class latents into target-class latents, which are decoded into target-class point clouds through the inverse flow. We adopt attacker-oriented metrics, including New-Class Recognition Rate (NCRR), Original-Class Leakage Rate (OCLR), and Original Label Recovery Rate (OLRR), to evaluate privacy and utility. Experiments on classification and segmentation benchmarks show that the proposed method achieves controllable semantic transformation, effectively reduces original-class semantic leakage, preserves downstream learnability in the protected domain, and supports reliable authorized reconstruction.

title: Federated Learning for Data Security and Trust in University Sports Systems
abstract: University sports information systems continuously aggregate data from fitness tests, courses, venue use, check-ins, and wearable devices—multi-source, heterogeneous, distributed, and privacy-sensitive data whose centralized modeling exposes students’ sports and health information, complicates cross-node collaboration, and limits scalability. We therefore build a secure, trustworthy federated learning mechanism for university sports information systems with a six-layer framework spanning data acquisition through application services. After local training it applies gradient pruning, differential-privacy perturbation, and secure aggregation, while node trustworthiness—from contribution, update stability, anomaly risk, and historical reputation—drives trust-weighted aggregation, coupling privacy protection with dynamic credibility control rather than treating them as independent modules. Under non-IID distributions, simulations show the method achieves accuracy, recall, F1, and AUC of 0.887, 0.873, 0.879, and 0.914, exceeding FedAvg’s F1 by about 5.8 points and DP-FedAvg’s by about 6.7; with 30% malicious nodes it still holds F1 = 0.831 versus 0.702 for FedAvg. The mechanism thus improves performance, privacy, and anomalous-node suppression without raw sports data leaving local nodes

title: The Effect of Effectively Integrating an Intelligent Virtual Companion into Active Learning Activities in the Computer Subject on Developing practical skills among fifth-grade students
abstract: هدفت هذه الدراسة إلى استكشاف أثر توظيف الرفيق الافتراضي في أنشطة التعلم النشط في مادة الحاسوب على المهارات العملية لدى طلبة الصف الخامس. ولتحقيق أهداف الدراسة تم اعتماد المنهج التجريبي بالتصميم شبه التجريبي. وتم اختيار مدرسة (المتنبي الابتدائية -مجد الكروم) بطريقة العينة القصدية الميسرة. واختيار شعبتين من شعب الصف الخامس اختياراً عشوائياً بسيطاً إحداهما تجريبية (ن= 24) والأخرى ضابطة (ن= 21). وتكونت أدوات جمع البيانات من بطاقة الملاحظة للمهارات العملية. وأظهرت نتائج الدراسة وجود فروق ذاتُ دلالة إحصائية في متوسط المهارات العملية لدى طلبة المجموعة التجريبية ولصالح القياس البعدي. ووجود فروق ذات دلالة إحصائية في متوسط المهارات العملية بين المجموعة التجريبية والمجموعة الضابطة ولصالح المجموعة التجريبية. وأوصت الدراسة بضرورة دمج أدوات تقييم رقمية مرتبطة بالرفيق الافتراضي لقياس التقدم في المهارات العملية والوجدانية بشكل متكامل.

title: Cross-Domain Multi-Semantic Trajectory Anomaly Detection via Kinematic Constraints and Bidirectional Sequential Reconstruction
abstract: To address the bottlenecks of weak cross-domain generalization, insufficient representation of complex spatial behaviors, and the scarcity of real anomaly labels in the detection of multi-semantic pedestrian trajectory anomalies (e.g., running, loitering, and wrong-way) in public security, this paper proposes an unsupervised detection framework combining kinematic constraints and a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory Autoencoder (Bi-LSTM-AE). While deep graph neural networks and attention-based models capture multi-agent interactions, they are frequently prone to spatial weight drift and severe computational overhead when transferred across disparate surveillance layouts. In contrast, our framework focuses on the intrinsic kinematic manifold of individual trajectories, striking an effective trade-off between cross-domain generalizability and linear computational complexity O(L). To this end, we construct a rigorous cross-domain evaluation paradigm, utilizing normal trajectories from a massive public dataset (SDD) to drive the unsupervised training of the model, aiming to fit a generalized human walking manifold unconstrained by specific physical scenes. To tackle the lack of multi-dimensional evaluation benchmarks, we design a multi-semantic anomaly generation strategy based on underlying kinematic constraints, programmatically synthesizing highly realistic challenging test samples on the ground-truth manifold of the target domain (UCY). Cross-domain experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework can overcome the Gaussian smoothing trap of generative models and the cross-domain generalization degradation of complex graph networks. In highly challenging unseen scenes, the overall detection F1 score is maintained above 0.90; notably, in the detection of “spatial loop anomalies (loitering)” that relies on a global spatio-temporal receptive field, a precise recall rate of 93.76% is achieved. With linear computational complexity, our method provides a novel solution for highly robust intelligent video surveillance early-warning in the open world.

title: Research with parallel corpora in the AI era
abstract: We introduce Vecalign, a novel bilingual sentence alignment method which is linear in time and space with respect to the number of sentences being aligned and which requires only bilingual sentence embeddings.On a standard German-French test set, Vecalign outperforms the previous state-of-the-art method (which has quadratic time complexity and requires a machine translation system) by 5 F 1 points.It substantially outperforms the popular Hunalign toolkit at recovering Bible verse alignments in medium-to low-resource language pairs, and it improves downstream MT quality by 1.7 and 1.6 BLEU in Sinhala→English and Nepali→English, respectively, compared to the Hunalign-based Paracrawl pipeline.

title: Integrated photonic neuromorphic computing: device, architecture, chip, and algorithm
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has advanced rapidly in recent years. In particular, the large AI models have been widely applied in fields such as natural language processing, image generation, and complex decision-making systems, reshaping technological paradigms across multiple industries. Nevertheless, the substantial data-processing demands of model training and inference have created significant computational bottlenecks. Traditional electronic chips based on the von Neumann architecture struggle to meet the increasing demands for computational capacity and energy efficiency as AI continues to advance. Photonic neuromorphic computing has emerged as a promising computing paradigm in the post-Moore era. By exploiting the high speed and broad bandwidth of photonic signal transmission, together with the low-power characteristics of optical devices, integrated photonic computing chips have the potential to alleviate the memory-wall and power-wall limitations of electronic computing systems. Recent years have witnessed substantial advances in photonic neuromorphic computing. This review presents a systematic review of the latest research achievements. It first introduces the fundamental principles and representative neuromorphic photonic devices, including photonic synapses and photonic neurons. It then summarizes photonic neural network architectures, integrated neuromorphic photonic chips, and optimization algorithms for photonic neural networks. Finally, based on the current status and major challenges of the field, this review discusses future directions in device integration, hardware–algorithm co-optimization, and the expansion of application scenarios, providing a perspective for further research in photonic neuromorphic computing.

title: A Panoramic-Image-Based Method for Recognizing Street Shade Conditions under Direct and Reflected Solar Radiation: Validation in Central Tokyo
abstract: As urbanization progresses and urban overheating intensifies, pedestrian-level shade conditions are becoming increasingly important for characterizing solar exposure in dense urban streets. However, existing methods remain limited in their ability to recognize detailed shade conditions, particularly when solar reflections from glass facades are involved. To address this gap, this study develops and validates a panoramic-image-based method for recognizing pedestrian-level shade conditions in urban streets, including tree shade, building shade, and conditions affected by reflected solar radiation. The proposed method generates tree and building masks from panoramic images and predicts glass locations through a geometric transformation approach. The direct and reflected radiation components are then determined by combining sun path and reflection path analyses using the panoramic images. The method was validated using walking survey data and three-dimensional laser-scanning data collected in a high-density district in central Tokyo, Japan. Across the 113 non-reference evaluation locations, the proposed glass location prediction method achieved mean Precision, Recall, and F1 scores of 91.3%, 81.6%, and 86.1%, respectively. The proposed shade condition recognition method also achieved high overall performance, with Macro-F1 scores of 84.7% across all examined shade conditions and 82.9% across the three reflection-related shade conditions. These findings demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively distinguish detailed pedestrian-level shade conditions in complex urban streets, thereby providing useful information for shade management and street design in high-density street-canyon environments.

title: Handcrafted features and ensemble learning for religious aggression detection in Bangla social media
abstract: Religious aggression on social media poses a growing threat to digital harmony and societal stability. In Bangladesh, where religion is deeply interwoven with cultural identity, online platforms often amplify intolerant and hostile discourse, fueling offline conflict. Automated detection of such aggression is therefore both a computational necessity and a social imperative. While hate speech detection in English has advanced considerably, Bangla, spoken by over 230 million people, remains critically under-resourced due to the lack of annotated corpora, linguistic complexity, and dialectal diversity. To address this gap, we introduce the Bangla Religious Aggression Comments (BRAC) dataset, comprising 20,000 manually annotated social media comments. Each comment is labeled along two dimensions: (i) whether it expresses religious aggression, and (ii) the specific religion targeted. Accordingly, we perform two sequential tasks: first, a binary classification to detect whether a comment is aggressive or non-aggressive, and second, a multi-class classification to identify the target religion, categorized as Muslim-AG (MAG), Hindu-AG (HAG), Christian-AG (CAG), and Buddhist-AG (BAG). We present the first comprehensive benchmark for this task, evaluating traditional machine learning, deep learning, and Transformer-based models. The proposed model is a soft-voting ensemble of XGBoost and Random Forest (XGB + RF) trained on TF–IDF features augmented with religion-word and offensive-word lexicon features. For aggression detection, the proposed ensemble achieves the highest accuracy (96.73%), while BanglaBERT attains the highest precision (95.55%) and F1-score (96.06%). For target religion classification, performance is comparable: the ensemble is slightly ahead in accuracy (94.67%), whereas BanglaBERT obtains the best F1-score (94.81%). These findings demonstrate complementary strengths between sparse lexical ensembles and contextual Transformer representations for domain-specific aggression detection in morphologically rich, low-resource languages such as Bangla.

title: Confidence-Gated Cloud-Edge Cascade Triage via Variational Risk Minimization for Medical Imaging
abstract: Emergency chest X-ray (CXR) triage has a structural modality gap: reports arrive after triage decisions, yet multimodal foundation models require image-text inputs. We present Variational Risk Minimization (VRM), a distillation framework that treats LVLM-generated report variants as Monte Carlo samples of latent clinical interpretations. Rather than distilling from a single teacher target, VRM learns from a variationally marginalized teacher distribution, enabling uncertainty-aware supervision under missing-modality constraints. Under matched encoder families, VRM outperforms direct fine-tuning baselines and improves calibration with strong recovery from hallucinated supervision. Marginalized supervision reduces report-selection instability. In our compact edge-student instantiation, a confidence-gated cascade reaches AUC 0.941 at 103ms average latency with 20.3% cloud escalation, yielding an explicit reliability-latency operating point for cloud-edge clinical workflows.

title: Learning SYK Hamiltonians
abstract: We study the problem of learning the dense Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (SYK) Hamiltonian from copies of its Gibbs state. Existing algorithms for Hamiltonian learning typically rely on geometric locality or bounded interaction degree and therefore do not apply to SYK, where each quartic interaction overlaps with $Θ(n^3)$ others. We show that this obstruction can be overcome by exploiting the random mean-field structure of the model. At any constant temperature, we prove that with high probability over the SYK couplings, the entire Hamiltonian can be learned to inverse-polynomial accuracy using polynomially many samples. Furthermore, when the inverse temperature is restricted to be a sufficiently small constant, we construct a quasipolynomial-time learning algorithm which is qualitatively different from the sample-efficient algorithm.

title: Constant-Per-Layer-Depth MPS-Pretrained Ansatz for Noisy Distributed Quantum Processors
abstract: Distributed quantum processors could scale variational algorithms beyond single devices, but circuit depth, communication overhead, and noise limit their performance. We compare ladder, mixed-canonical, and brick-wall realizations of matrix-product-state (MPS) pretraining with matched per-layer two-qubit-block resources. Despite comparable ideal variational quantum eigensolver performance and gradient scales, the shallower brick-wall architecture reduces circuit duration, idle-time decoherence, and zero-noise-extrapolation (ZNE) overhead, yielding superior noisy and ZNE-assisted performance. We then extend MPS-pretrained circuits to modular processors with one communication qubit per quantum processing unit (QPU); a nearest-neighbor QPU-path schedule keeps the per-layer depth constant as QPUs are added. Distributed circuits whose inter-QPU links realize long-range interactions of the target Hamiltonian match or outperform the single-processor brick-wall under noise when communication idle time is short compared with the coherence time. These results establish hardware-aware co-design of tensor-network pretraining, circuit scheduling, and communication topology as a principle for variational quantum computation on noisy modular hardware.

title: Beyond Answer Confidence: A Controlled Audit of Self-Knowledge in a Black-Box Decision Model
abstract: Decision models return probabilities intended for routing, abstention and automated action. Calibration makes those probabilities useful on average, but does not establish whether low confidence reflects chance or missing knowledge, nor whether confidence falls when a model moves beyond what it knows. We audit this distinction in Jev, a decision model, with over 15 public datasets and 6 generated task families, with paired interventions that vary the information supplied for a fixed item. Jev's confidence is calibrated on familiar closed-choice tasks but fails as an indicator of missing knowledge: with no answer-relevant information it assigns up to 0.80 to a salient option, and on news beyond an observed knowledge boundary it exceeds accuracy by 0.21--0.33, a gap that recalibration on earlier months does not close. Targeted yes/no questions give sharper readouts of the case: whether an outcome is settled (AUROC 1.00) and whether the evidence suffices (0.95, against 0.85 for confidence on the same items). Asking whether Jev knows the answer appears to flag fabricated entities and post-boundary news (0.91), but with realistic names or with dates removed it shows no advantage over answer uncertainty. Black-box knowledge audits therefore need explicit controls for surface cues. Code: https://github.com/Syntheme/beyond-answer-confidence.

title: Androw of Aces: Mitigating Autoregressive Arithmetic Drift in Large Language Models via Canonical Pre-Sorting and Key-Value Bound Binary Prefix-Sum Scratchpads
abstract: Autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs) frequently fail at multi-variable arithmetic aggregation when operating in-context without external code execution. Bounded by circuit complexity class $\mathsf{TC}^0$, standard transformers struggle with sequential carry states across lists of length $N > 3$, suffering from copy-alignment drift. This work introduces Androw of Aces (ACES), a lightweight in-context execution protocol enforcing four invariants: an Autoregressive Conditional Gate ($N > 3$), Canonical Pre-Sorting, Explicit Key-Value Parenthetical Binding, and Sequential Binary Subtotaling. By unrolling multi-term sums into an entity-anchored $\Theta(N)$ prefix-sum scratchpad, ACES achieves zero-variance arithmetic aggregation natively in conversational interfaces.

title: Data from Radiometer (RAD) measurements at Paris – Compiègne (PACOMP) from 2023-01-27 to 2024-03-25 [L0]
abstract: Combined and uncalibrated logger data from radiometer measurements on a sun tracker with global, direct and diffuse shortwave irradiance and longwave irradiance Paris – Compiègne (PACOMP) (Départment 60) in the rural region to the NNE of Greater Paris recorded during the urbisphere Paris Campaign from 2023-01-27 00:00 to 2024-03-26 00:00 UTC. Measuerments were taken on the roof of the Université de Technologie de Compiègne at 49.40138°N / 2.80132°E. The L0 datafile combines all individual uncalibrated logger files (automatic transfer, manual download) with a consistent and consecutive time axis. Missing data is filled with -9999. The data file has each time step as a row and each parameter as a column in comma-separated csv format. The columns contain readings converted to physical units with simple quality control from all radiometers and a co-located all-in one automatic weather station (AWS). The file PACOMP-MET_1min-202301270000_202403260000_UTC.csv has the format of a comma-separated .csv file with 4 header lines following the Campbell Scientific Inc. TOA5 file definition. The L0 data combined all raw data files into a single .csv file covering the entire period of observations at PACOMP from 2023-01-27 13:14 to 2024-03-26 11:26 UTC based on RAW data averaged every minute. RAW data (individual logger output files) can be found here: Morrison, W., Antaluca, E., Hilland, R., Looschelders, D., Zeeman, M., Grimmond, S., & Christen, A. (2024). Data from Radiometer (RAD) measurements at Paris – Compiègne (PACOMP) from 2023-01-27 to 2024-03-25 [RAW] (Version v1.0.2) [Dataset]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.12967512 Radiation measurements taken at PACOMP are: Direct normal irradiance (DNI) with an CHP1 pyrheliometer Global (solar) hemispherical irradiance (GHI) with an actively ventilated Kipp&Zonen CM21 pyranometer Diffuse (solar) irradiance with an actively ventilated and shaded Kipp&Zonen CM21 pyranometer Longwave hemispherical irradiance (LHI) with an actively ventilated and shaded Kipp&Zonen CG1 pyrgeometer All radiation fluxes are measured using a sun tracker (Kipp & Zonen SOLYS2) and continuously ventilated instruments. Further, the dataset contains simple meteorological measurements of barometric pressure, wind velocity, wind direction, air temperature, humidity, precipitation and lightning using a all-in-one weather station (Campbell Scientific ClimaVue 50) installed next to the sun tracker. The dataset is calibrated using manufacturer calibrations for all instruments and no further quality controlls or gap filling procedures have been applied. For quality controlled and calibrated data use L2 data instead. evidence.abstract: Combined and uncalibrated logger data from radiometer measurements on a sun tracker with global, direct and diffuse shortwave irradiance and longwave irradiance Paris – Compiègne (PACOMP) (Départment 60) in the rural region to the NNE of Greater Paris recorded during the urbisphere Paris Campaign from 2023-01-27 00:00 to 2024-03-26 00:00 UTC. Measuerments were taken on the roof of the Université de Technologie de Compiègne at 49.40138°N / 2.80132°E. The L0 datafile combines all individual uncalibrated logger files (automatic transfer, manual download) with a consistent and consecutive time axis. Missing data is filled with -9999. The data file has each time step as a row and each parameter as a column in comma-separated csv format. The columns contain readings converted to physical units with simple quality control from all radiometers and a co-located all-in one automatic weather station (AWS). The file PACOMP-MET_1min-202301270000_202403260000_UTC.csv has the format of a comma-separated .csv file with 4 header lines following the Campbell Scientific Inc. TOA5 file definition. The L0 data combined all raw data files into a single .csv file covering the entire period of observations at PACOMP from 2023-01-27 13:14 to 2024-03-26 11:26 UTC based on RAW data averaged every minute. RAW data (individual logger output files) can be found here: Morrison, W., Antaluca, E., Hilland, R., Looschelders, D., Zeeman, M., Grimmond, S., & Christen, A. (2024).
